settings.heading: Size the driver properly. It is the part that fails first.
settings.subheading: Enter your run length and the strip's watts per metre. We add 20% headroom and tell you which 24V driver to buy.

settings.heading: Length × watts per metre, plus 20%.
settings.text: Multiply your strip length by its rated watts per metre — 12W/m on KAYVA 480 Pro — then add 20% headroom so the driver isn't running at full capacity. A driver running flat-out runs hot and fails early. Check the W/m figure on your strip's spec sheet; generic strip is often rated optimistically.

settings.wpm_hint: Printed on the reel or the spec sheet. If a listing quotes only total watts for a 5 m reel, divide by 5.

settings.note: Recalculates with the watts per metre you set above.
settings.footnote: For runs 6 m and longer, power the strip from both ends or split it into segments with separate feeds. This prevents voltage drop, where the far end of a long run appears dimmer than the start.

settings.title: 24V constant voltage
settings.text: Not constant current, not 12V. Constant-current drivers will not run strip correctly.

settings.title: TRIAC-dimmable, if dimming
settings.text: The strip does not dim on its own — the driver does. Pair it with a compatible wall dimmer.

settings.title: Licensed electrician for mains
settings.text: Required in Singapore. The low-voltage side — driver to strip — is safe to handle unpowered.

settings.heading: Send us the cove length. We will spec the driver.
settings.text: Message us on WhatsApp with your run lengths and whether it is on a dimmer. No obligation.
